Two pickers stop naming the act of resolving and simply show the answer.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The language list has no "Automatic" row.** It even carried the resolved flag, which made it look like the thoughtful version, and it still could not answer the question anybody opens that screen to ask: which language am I reading. The list now marks the language actually in effect, from the first time it is opened, whether or not anything has been chosen. Picking one still overrides it, as before.
- **The theme picker offers light and dark, and starts on whatever the device is set to.** The third chip named the act of resolving rather than a result, so the control could not say which of the two was running. Nothing is stored until a side is picked, so a device that switches to dark in the evening still takes the app with it.

## 📋 Notes

- Both changes are the same rule, and it lives in the shared design language now rather than in one surface's head: an option that describes how a value is found is not an option, it is an excuse for not showing the value. The browser extension had already been corrected; this app had not, which is exactly what a rule written down in one place is supposed to prevent.
- Two translation keys are gone from all 42 languages with them.
